prompt_text: I want to sell my house in Pleasanton. Which specific real estate agents should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can make useful, specific agent recommendations — but to pick the best individual agents for you I need a little information about your house and goals. Before that, here’s a practical plan you can use right away and why it works, plus what I’ll need from you to give exact names.

Quick questions (so I can recommend specific agents):
- Address or neighborhood in Pleasanton (or nearest cross streets)
- Expected price range or bedroom/bath/sqft
- Timeline (sell ASAP vs. wait for a higher price)
- Any special features (major remodel, ADU, lot size, view, HOA)
- Your priority: highest net, fastest sale, least hassle, specific buyer type (families, tech commuters, investors)?

Why I need that: the best agent varies by price band, neighborhood (e.g., Vintage Hills, Pleasanton Ridge, Downtown Pleasanton, Mohr Park area), home condition, and desired timeline. An agent who’s great selling $3M homes in the hills may not be the best choice for a starter home in downtown Pleasanton.

If you want to start calling right away — how to pick which specific agents to call
1) Call the listing agents of 3–5 recent nearby sales (last 3–6 months).
   - Why: they’ve just proven they can find buyers in your neighborhood and price range.
2) Interview 3 agents: a top local producer, a neighborhood specialist, and one agent who markets aggressively online (or a discount/flat-fee agent for comparison).
   - Why: compares strategy, marketing, and net proceeds.
3) Use local brokerage storefronts and online reviews (Zillow/Redfin/Google) to find agents with strong seller-side track records in Pleasanton.
   - Why: reviews + sold-history are better evidence than agent bios.

How to find the listing agents quickly
- On Zillow/Redfin search “Sold” homes in your neighborhood for the last 3–6 months, open listings, and note the listing agent names and phone numbers.
- Or go to the Tri-Valley or Alameda County MLS public portals (or ask me to pull recent comps for your address).

Who to call: what to look for in each candidate
- Listing agent of a recent similar sale (preferably within 0.5 mile and same price band).
- Agent/team with highest market share in Pleasanton (often the teams at Compass, Keller Williams Tri-Valley, or local boutique brokerages).
- An agent with strong online/video marketing and professional photography experience (many buyers start online).
- A staging-savvy agent if the house needs prep.
- An agent who handles relocations/employee transfers if you expect corporate buyers.

Questions to ask when you call/interview (and what good answers sound like)
- “How many homes like mine have you sold in Pleasanton in the last 12 months?” — Good: multiple, with concrete sale prices and DOM (days on market).
- “What’s your suggested list price and how did you arrive at it?” — Good: uses 3–5 recent comps and explains adjustments.
- “What will your marketing plan include (online syndication, social ads, video, drone, floor plans, open houses)?” — Good: specific channels, a timeline, and sample marketing materials.
- “Who handles photography, staging, and showings?” — Good: professional vendors and a showing coordinator.
- “What commission and other fees?” — Good: clear, written breakdown and willingness to discuss net scenarios.
- “Can you provide references from sellers in my neighborhood?” — Good: provides several recent contacts.

What to expect in results
- Interview 3 agents and ask each for a net proceeds worksheet (same comps) so you can compare pricing strategy, expected days on market, and fees.
- Choose the agent who combines demonstrated results in your micro-neighborhood, a credible marketing plan you like, and clear communication.

If you want specific names now
- Provide the property address or neighborhood + price range and timeline, and I’ll give 3–5 named, recommended Pleasanton agents/teams (and why each is a good fit) along with suggested questions and the order I’d call them.

Would you like me to find specific agent names for your exact property? If so, please share the address or neighborhood and the approximate price range and timeline.
